name: Glaucoma secondary to spherophakia, ectopia lentis, and megalocornea
aliases: Secondary glaucoma due to spherophakia and lens dislocation
Glaucoma associated with megalocornea and ectopia lentis

criteria.description: Presence of spherophakia characterized by a small, spherical crystalline lens
Ectopia lentis demonstrated by lens subluxation or dislocation
Megalocornea defined as an abnormally enlarged corneal diameter (>13 mm)
Elevated intraocular pressure consistent with glaucoma
Optic nerve head cupping and visual field defects consistent with glaucomatous optic neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of spherophakia or ectopia lentis combined with megalocornea and clinical evidence of glaucoma (elevated intraocular pressure and optic nerve damage)
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by ophthalmologic imaging and pressure measurements.

pathognomonic.notes: Spherical, small crystalline lens causing refractive abnormalities
Displacement of the lens from its normal position
Enlarged corneal diameter exceeding normal limits

common.notes: Increased pressure within the eye leading to optic nerve damage
Loss of peripheral vision typical of glaucomatous damage
Nearsightedness caused by altered lens shape
searchTerms: blurred distance vision due to lens
myopia caused by lens shape issues

common.notes: Irregular corneal curvature contributing to visual distortion

occasional.notes: Swelling of the cornea secondary to elevated intraocular pressure
Light sensitivity due to corneal or lens abnormalities
Visual phenomenon related to corneal edema or lens changes
Occasional ocular discomfort related to increased pressure

rare.notes: Sudden increase in intraocular pressure causing severe symptoms
searchTerms: episodes of painful high eye pressure

rare.notes: Iris tremor due to lens instability
searchTerms: tremulous movement of colored eye part
cloudy lens after surgery or trauma

imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing spherophakia and ectopia lentis
Gonioscopy revealing narrow or closed angles
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrating optic nerve head cupping
Ultrasound biomicroscopy for lens position assessment
other: Visual field testing showing characteristic glaucomatous defects

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of lens abnormalities such as spherophakia or ectopia lentis
Typically presents in infancy with buphthalmos
Systemic features including skeletal and cardiovascular abnormalities
Ectopia lentis present but megalocornea uncommon
Genetic testing positive for FBN1 mutations
Spherophakia and ectopia lentis present but typically microcornea rather than megalocornea

redFlags: Severe ocular pain with nausea or vomiting (suggestive of acute angle-closure glaucoma)
Marked asymmetry in intraocular pressure or optic nerve damage between eyes
references: Orphanet: Glaucoma secondary to spherophakia/ectopia lentis and megalocornea (ORPHA:238763)
Kumar A, et al. Spherophakia and secondary glaucoma: clinical features and management. Eye (Lond). 2019.
Weiss AH, et al. Lens abnormalities and glaucoma: pathophysiology and treatment. Surv Ophthalmol. 2021.
